title: The notebook your orders are written in
summary: Orders in Supermarket Simulator are kept in a notebook of its own: the game holds the notebook in a container, gives it a display and an animation, sets how orders spawn, and can call a vehicle for a delivery.
body: What you have ordered is kept in a notebook rather than in your head. The game holds that notebook in a container of its own, which is why the list of orders survives leaving the screen and coming back.
The notebook is shown, not only stored. It has a display of its own, so the same record can be put in front of you as something you look at rather than a list of numbers.
It moves like an object. The notebook has an animation of its own, which is why opening and closing it is a movement rather than the list appearing out of nothing.
How orders arrive is set separately. There is a settings object for how orders spawn, so when an order appears is a thing the game decides rather than a consequence of the notebook being open.
A delivery can be called for. The game can request a vehicle, which is how a large order is collected rather than carried.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the order icon it draws, which is what the notebook is a record of.
What this entry does not tell you: how many orders can wait at once, how long a delivery takes, or what a delivery costs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Orders are kept in a notebook held in a container of its own.
The notebook has a display of its own.
It has an animation of its own.
How orders spawn is set by a settings object of its own.
A vehicle can be requested for a delivery.
The game ships its own icon for an online order.
